title: Fresh Summer Corn Chowder
headnote: Velvety corn chowder made with a homemade fresh-cob corn stock, crispy thick bacon, Yukon Gold potatoes, and chives. “Simmering the stripped cobs in the broth and cream creates an unbelievably rich, naturally sweet corn stock that elevates this chowder.” — Bob Mitchell

quotes.text: Simmering the stripped cobs in the broth and cream creates an unbelievably rich, naturally sweet corn stock that elevates this chowder.
quotes.span: “Simmering the stripped cobs in the broth and cream creates an unbelievably rich, naturally sweet corn stock that elevates this chowder.” — Bob Mitchell

items.raw: 4 cups fresh corn kernels (5 to 6 ears) — keep the cobs

steps.text: Cut the kernels from the cobs and set them aside for the chowder. Put the bare cobs in a stockpot — snap them in half if they do not fit.

Add the chicken broth, milk, and cream to the cobs. Bring just to a boil — watch it, milk boils over fast — then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Lift out and discard the cobs with tongs.
In a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat, cook the bacon until crisp. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the onion and carrot to the bacon fat and sauté uncovered until softened, 7 to 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, the reserved corn kernels, 2 teaspoons of the salt, the black pepper, and the cayenne.
Pour in the warm corn stock. Bring to a light boil, then simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Taste and season with the remaining salt and more pepper.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with the crispy bacon and chopped chives.

notes.label: Don’t throw out the cobs
notes.text: simmering them is the secret to deep corn flavor.

notes.label: Bacon fat
notes.text: cooking the vegetables in it gives the whole chowder its smoky base.

notes.label: Thicker chowder
notes.text: purée about 2 cups in a blender and stir it back in.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: even better the next day. Reheat gently; a hard boil can make the dairy grainy.
